concept: Compound III Comet and Euler v2 vault kit
summary: Source-anchored research for Compound III Comet and Euler v2 vault kit. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: A Compound III (Comet) deployment is an isolated market with exactly one borrowable base asset (the original market is USDC on Ethereum, cUSDCv3). Users post other listed assets as collateral and borrow only the base asset; only base-asset suppliers earn interest. (high confidence)

Comet is a small set of contracts. The Comet core (inherits CometMainInterface) forwards unrecognised function selectors to CometExt by delegatecall; the Configurator (behind a TransparentUpgradeableProxy-derived ConfiguratorProxy) holds configuration and deploys new Comet implementations through CometFactory; CometProxyAdmin adds deployAndUpgradeTo, which deploys a new Comet and upgrades the proxy in one transaction; Bulker batches calls and CometRewards handles reward claims. (high confidence)

Euler v2 has two layers. The Euler Vault Kit (EVK) builds 'credit vaults': ERC-4626 vaults with added borrowing functionality that act as passive lending pools and do not invest deposits. The Ethereum Vault Connector (EVC) is a foundational layer between vaults: the EVC is responsible for authentication and vaults for authorisation, and each vault holds a single asset. (high confidence)
MixBytes notes that fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens are unsupported by Euler v2 vaults because vaults track balances internally. (low confidence)

To vet an Euler vault before depositing, check the factory that deployed it, whether it is upgradeable or finalised (governor set to address(0)), which perspective verifies it, its oracle and unit of account, and which other vaults' shares it accepts as collateral. (medium confidence)

Euler risk configuration is per vault. Collateral is risk-adjusted by LTV factors, the borrowing LTV must be less than or equal to the liquidation LTV, and LTV ramps affect only liquidation LTVs (new borrows use the new value immediately). (medium confidence)

Design contrast: Compound III is a governance-run product, with fixed single-base-asset deployments whose parameters change only through Timelock proposals. Euler v2 is a permissionless toolkit where anyone can deploy vaults and each vault's governor or curator sets risk. Euler's then-CEO Michael Bentley framed it as 'You can use Euler to build other lending protocols, but the reverse isn't true'. (medium confidence)

EVC batch() executes several operations atomically and lets account-status and vault-status checks run once, deferred to the end of the call context. Users are expected to go through the EVC's call or batch rather than calling vaults directly, so sub-account and operator authorisation applies. MixBytes likewise describes the EVC as managing accounts, operators and multicalls. (medium confidence)

Comet enforces a minimum borrow size, baseBorrowMin: an account's initial borrow must be at least that value, a withdrawal that would leave the borrow below it reverts, and later borrows may be any size. Governance can change the borrow minimum through the Configurator. (medium confidence)

OpenZeppelin's medium findings show Comet's trust edges: approveThis let the governor approve anyone to move base and collateral assets out of Comet (a governance-attack vector; docstrings were clarified), and a low targetReserves value could stop buyCollateral and leave the protocol holding collateral (the team said targetReserves is meant to be 'a pretty large value'). The governance docs confirm that only the Governor can withdraw reserves or approve manager allowances. (medium confidence)

Anyone can deploy EVK vault proxies through the factory; EVault dispatches some logic to static modules. Upgradeable vaults point at a factory-controlled beacon and immutable vaults use a fixed implementation. A governor can change vault configuration, and setting the governor to address(0) finalises the vault. 'Perspectives' are verifier contracts; the escrowed-collateral perspective requires no borrowing, immutability and finalisation. At launch Euler's frontend supported four vault classes: escrowed collateral, governed, ungoverned and yield aggregator. (high confidence)
